subject: Proposal: rolling-year cap and carve-outs — MSA & Order Form
summary: Coordination of MSA redlines focusing on limitation of liability: proposing a rolling 12-month cap (annual reset) tied to fees paid, with carve-outs for indemnity and gross negligence. Collecting internal legal feedback and aligning on fallback language for per-claim vs aggregate exposure.
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: rolling-year cap and carve-outs — MSA & Order Form

Anna — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is a short proposal and the redline (BL_Redline_MSA_v3.docx) that implements the items we discussed. The core idea we want to float so your team can react to is: 1) move to a rolling 12-month (annual-reset) cap rather than a single cumulative cap across the contract term, and 2) define the cap as the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (b) a fixed multiple of the initial year fee (we've proposed 2x initial year fees as a starting point).

Rationale (brief):
- Rolling-year caps align with BrightLeaf's usage seasonality and give both parties a predictable annual exposure number.
- Tying to fees paid gives commercial alignment — larger customers with higher spend get higher caps.
- We want clear carve-outs for statutory remedies, claims subject to indemnity (IP infringement), and damages arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Open items we want your legal team to evaluate:
- Do you have objections to annual reset vs. cumulative? If you need a cumulative floor for the term, what's an acceptable multiplier?
- Is the proposed 2x initial year fee reasonable as a ceiling for low-usage ramp customers?
- Carve-outs language: BrightLeaf asked us to confirm consequential damages carve-out. We propose excluding consequential, incidental, and punitive damages except for those carved back in by indemnity or breach of confidentiality.

Please review the attached redline and the short order form adjustment. If it helps, we can provide alternate wording that keeps a per-incident sub-cap + an aggregate rolling cap.

Attachment: BL_Redline_MSA_v3.docx (redline)
Attachment: OrderForm_2025-05-01.xlsx (fees schedule)

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@brightleaf.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2025-05-02T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rolling-year cap and carve-outs — MSA & Order Form

Vanessa — appreciate the write-up and the redline. High-level reaction from BrightLeaf Legal / Procurement:

1) Annual reset: acceptable in principle, but we need a guarantee that we won't see an effective reduction in recovery across a multi-year term. In other words, if a major incident occurs late in year 2 that consumes the year-2 cap, we want to preserve ability to recover for damages attributable to year 1 usage if caused by the same root failure.

2) Fees-tied cap: we prefer a minimum floor (e.g., no less than 1x annual committed fees) to avoid very low caps during pilot/introductory pricing periods.

3) Multiplier: 2x initial year fee is reasonable as a starting point for negotiation; procurement would like an option to test 3x for enterprise support situations, but that's secondary.

4) Carve-outs: we agree on carve-outs for indemnity and gross negligence. We also want to keep a carve-back for breach of data processing obligations (PII exposure). On consequential damages, we need clearer examples in the MSA rather than open-ended lists.

We're sending this back to our GC for a closer read. In parallel, procurement would like a short side-letter that documents the annual-reset mechanics and an example calculation. Do you have a template?

On timing: can we aim to resolve the cap language within the week so procurement can progress the commercial terms?

Best — Anna
Anna Brooks
Head of Legal Operations, BrightLeaf Analytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-03T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: rolling-year cap and carve-outs — MSA & Order Form

Vanessa / Karthik — quick internal legal take after reviewing Anna's note and the redline:

- Annual-reset mechanics: we should add a paragraph that clarifies cross-year causation. Wording suggestion: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, to the extent a single incident or series of related incidents spans multiple 12-month periods, the Parties will aggregate amounts attributable to that incident when determining recoverable damages, subject to the aggregate cap for the relevant rolling period(s)." This addresses BrightLeaf's concern about late-term incidents.

- Floor for pilots: accept a floor of 1x committed fees in the first 12 months. For true trial pilots (no committed fees), propose a nominal floor of $25,000.

- Multiplier: keep 2x as baseline, allow uplift to 3x upon execution of premium support addendum. We should surface that commercial option to Sales so they can choose during negotiation.

- Carve-outs: tighten the consequential damages definition by adding examples limited to lost profits, business interruption, and third-party consequential claims, and explicitly carve back data breach and IP indemnity. Also add a survival clause for indemnity obligations.

I've added tracked changes to BL_Redline_MSA_v3.docx (see comments in the doc). Also flagged a cross-ref in OrderForm_2025-05-01.xlsx where the "initial year fee" calculation needs to be defined (is it committed MRR * 12 or invoice run-rate?).

If you want, I can draft the side-letter for the annual-reset example and attach a short calculation template.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: rolling-year cap and carve-outs — MSA & Order Form

Anna — thanks for the quick turnaround and helpful feedback. We've incorporated Laura's clarifications and prepared a short side-letter example that walks through a sample incident spanning two rolling periods (attached).

Next steps I propose:
- I will share the updated redline + a 1-page side-letter with calculation template by EOD today.
- If BrightLeaf GC is OK with the proposed cross-year aggregation language, procurement can proceed and Sales will confirm whether the customer wants premium support (3x multiplier) or baseline (2x).
- If GC pushes back on annual reset categorically, fallback is to offer a cumulative cap equal to 2.5x initial year fees (commercial only) — we prefer to avoid embedding that as the default.

Let me know if you want a quick call tomorrow morning to walk through the example.

Thanks — Vanessa
